review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the uses of the simp-relevant lemmas inside it. I also looked at how Mathlib tags pullback.lift_fst/lift_snd (@[reassoc] only, not simp) and ΓSpecIso_inv_naturality (@[reassoc (attr := simp)]). The file contains no simp attributes at all, so I found no competing rules or rewrite cycles. All three findings are about missing interface pieces. They are not about wrong rewrite directions. I could not run Lean, so I did not test whether the proposed attributes would work. The effect on the downstream `solution` proof is judged by reading it. The reassoc and simp suggestions follow Mathlib conventions but are not tested.

findings.declaration: proj_def / fstL_def / sndL_def (and the parallel pairs D_map_fst vs D_map_fstL, c_π_fst vs proj_fstL)
findings.excerpt: theorem fstL_def (L : FinIF k K) : pullback.fst fX (gF k K L) = fstL fX L := rfl
findings.problem: `proj`, `fstL` and `sndL` are plain `def`s, so `pullback.fst fX (gF k K L)` and `fstL fX L` are two different syntactic normal forms. The file therefore has two lemma families for the same facts: `D_map_fst`/`D_map_snd`/`c_π_fst`/`c_π_snd` use the raw vocabulary, and `D_map_fstL`/`D_map_sndL`/`proj_fstL`/`proj_sndL` use the wrapper vocabulary. The `_def` bridge lemmas are never used and are not simp lemmas. Consequently the main proof repeatedly falls back on `change` to convert between the two forms, and `rw` or `simp` cannot move between them.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one canonical form. Either make `proj`, `fstL` and `sndL` `abbrev`s, as the file already does for `gF` and `gK`. Then the L-lemmas also fire on the raw terms and the `_def` lemmas and `change` steps become unnecessary. Or keep the defs, declare the simp normal form explicitly, and tag the `_def` lemmas (or the raw-vocabulary lemmas) accordingly. State each fact only once.
findings.benefit: The simplifier and `rw` see a single normal form, so the duplicated lemma pairs and the unused `_def` lemmas go away. The `change fstL fX M ≫ fX = …` and `change G N hMN ≫ liftAt … ≫ sndL fX N = _` steps in `solution` no longer need to bridge the two vocabularies by hand.

findings.declaration: D_obj, D_map_fst, D_map_snd, c_π_fst, c_π_snd (against the `dsimp only [c, D, …]` uses)
findings.excerpt:
theorem D_map_fst {i j : (FinIF k K)ᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j) :
    (D k K X fX).map f ≫ pullback.fst fX (gF k K j.unop) = pullback.fst fX (gF k K i.unop) :=
findings.problem: The file proves the defining equations of the functor `D` and the cone `c` (`D_obj`, `D_map_fst`, `D_map_snd`, `c_π_fst`, `c_π_snd`). None of them is tagged `@[simp]` or `@[reassoc]`, and no `@[simps]` is used on `D` or `c`. Proofs instead unfold the whole definitions with `simp only [..., D]` and `dsimp only [c, D, Opposite.unop_op]`. This expands to the raw `pullback.map` and `pullback.lift` terms, which is unwanted expansion. Afterwards the proofs need manual `Category.assoc` and `← Category.assoc` rewriting. The `_assoc` variants that would avoid this are not generated.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `D_obj` as `@[simp]`. Mark `D_map_fst`, `D_map_snd`, `c_π_fst` and `c_π_snd` as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`. Each has `Functor.map` or `π.app` composed with a projection as its LHS and a simpler term on the RHS, so there is no loop. Then replace the `dsimp only [c, D]` steps in `isLimitCone` (and similar ones elsewhere) by `simp`, `rw [D_map_fst_assoc]` or similar, so the definitions of `D` and `c` stay folded.
findings.benefit: Proofs about `D` and `c` can use the interface lemmas instead of unfolding the constructions. This is more robust to changes in `D` and `c` and shortens the manual assoc bookkeeping.

findings.declaration: liftL_fstL, liftL_sndL (and liftAt_fstL, liftAt_sndL, D_map_fstL, D_map_sndL)
findings.excerpt: theorem liftL_fstL (L : FinIF k K) {W : Scheme.{0}} (a : W ⟶ X) (b : W ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L.1))
findings.problem: The projection equations for the wrapper `liftL`/`liftAt` and the transition maps `D.map` are the computation rules of this API. They exist only as plain theorems, with no `@[reassoc]` or simp attribute. This is a missing canonical simp interface. `liftL` and `liftAt` are defs, so Mathlib's `pullback.lift_fst` cannot fire on them. Every use therefore needs a hand-written `rw` with `Category.assoc` and `← Category.assoc`. Examples are the long chains in `liftAt_map`, `proj_liftAt`, `hGfst`/`hHfst` and `hGH_N`/`hHG_N`, where the order of the associativity rewrites has to be tracked by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `liftL_fstL`, `liftL_sndL`, `liftAt_fstL`, `liftAt_sndL`, `D_map_fstL` and `D_map_sndL` as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`. Their RHS is a strictly smaller expression, so they terminate. Then `simp [Category.assoc]` or the `_assoc` variants can replace the manual `rw [Category.assoc, liftAt_fstL, ← Category.assoc, …]` chains. The result is a canonical normal form where compositions with `fstL` and `sndL` are pushed through `liftL`, `liftAt` and `D.map`.
findings.benefit: Proofs of `liftAt_map`, `proj_liftAt`, `hGfst`/`hHfst` and `hGH_N`/`hHG_N` shorten and become less sensitive to associativity bracketing. Users of this API get ready-made simp and reassoc lemmas, as Mathlib provides for `pullback.lift_fst` (which has `@[reassoc]`).
